source_anchors.operation: Ratio::description_ is a public std::vector<std::string> that nothing in the SDK writes; the struct's own @TODO at line 106 notes that its members are public and should not end in underscores
operator<<(std::ostream&, const ConsensusFeature&) is declared as a free function, not a member

the printed block opens with "---------- CONSENSUS ELEMENT BEGIN -----------------" and closes at line 415 with "---------- CONSENSUS ELEMENT END ----------------- ", whose literal ends in a space before the newline
Position is streamed through DPosition's operator<<, which writes the coordinates space-separated: RT then m/z
"Intensity " and "Quality " (line 396) carry no colon while every other label does, and both values go through precisionWrapper
"Grouped features: " ends in a space inside the literal, as "Meta information: " does at line 408
the handles are printed in HandleSetType order (FeatureHandle::IndexLess: map index then unique ID), five indented lines each, not in insertion order
getKeys yields meta value names in MetaInfoRegistry index order, i.e. the order the process first registered each name; the port's BTreeMap prints them sorted
the operator prints no ratios at all, so Ratio and its description have no place in the stream output
DPosition's operator<< writes precisionWrapper(pos[0]) and then a space before each further coordinate
precisionWrapper sets the stream precision to writtenDigits<T>, which is digits10: 6 for float, 15 for double (CONCEPT/Types.h:178-195); this port writes Rust's shortest round-trip form instead

the class test's 39 sections cover the constructors, the insert overloads, the ranges, the three consensus computations and the container accessors; none of them exercises operator<<, Ratio::description_, addRatio, setRatios or getRatios, so the two members ported here have no upstream section
